title: 3rd Stopping Place 3rd Truth The Truth Of Disposing And Administering

questions.question: What is the main truth named in this passage?
questions.answer: It is the truth that Allah manages and governs creation.

questions.question: What kinds of things are included in this management?
questions.answer: It includes the huge bodies in the sky, the powerful natural elements, and the weak and needy creatures on earth.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the world under this rule?
questions.answer: It describes the world as being run like a perfect kingdom, a great city, and a beautiful palace.

questions.question: Why does the passage use an example instead of explaining everything about this rule?
questions.answer: Because the full subject is very vast, so one example from spring is used to show one clear part of it.

questions.question: In the comparison, what kind of leader is imagined?
questions.answer: A remarkable ruler who gathers a very large army from many different groups and peoples.

questions.question: About how many different groups are in that army?
questions.answer: Four hundred thousand.

questions.question: What must that ruler provide for each group?
questions.answer: He must give each one its own clothing, weapons, orders, release, and pay.

questions.question: What qualities mark the ruler’s management in the comparison?
questions.answer: It is done completely, correctly, on time, without mistakes, delay, shortage, or confusion.

questions.question: According to the comparison, what would happen if ordinary causes tried to do this work?
questions.answer: They would fail and spoil the balance by causing disorder.

questions.question: What real-world scene is this comparison pointing to?
questions.answer: It points to the way an unseen hand brings forth and manages countless living species every spring.

questions.question: What happens in autumn to many plant and animal species?
questions.answer: About three hundred thousand of them are dismissed from their duties and pass away.

questions.question: What action stands at the center of this passage?
questions.answer: The central action is orderly governing and arranging creation.

questions.question: Which three broad parts of creation are mentioned together at the start?
questions.answer: The heavenly bodies, the natural elements, and the creatures living on earth.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the relationship among these parts?
questions.answer: They are made to help one another and are managed together.

questions.question: What does this teach about the order of the world?
questions.answer: It teaches that the world is not random but carefully directed.

questions.question: In the example of the army, why is the task so amazing?
questions.answer: Because each group is different and still receives exactly what it needs in the right way and at the right time.

questions.question: Name two things that must be given separately to each group in the army example.
questions.answer: Their clothing and weapons.

questions.question: What does the passage say proves the greatness of the commander in the comparison?
questions.answer: The fact that such a huge and detailed system is handled perfectly proves extraordinary power.

questions.question: Why can no other hand share in this administration, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because any interfering cause would upset the balance and create confusion.

questions.question: What do people directly observe each spring, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They observe an unseen hand creating and managing a vast living army of many species.

questions.question: How is autumn compared to a day of resurrection in the passage?
questions.answer: It is presented as a time when many living things are sent away from their worldly duties through death.

questions.question: What title is given to the truth explained in this section?
questions.answer: It is called the truth of disposing and administering.

questions.question: What contrast appears between the beings mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: The passage mentions both mighty things, like heavenly bodies and elements, and weak creatures on earth.

questions.question: How is the whole world pictured after being managed this way?
questions.answer: It is pictured as an organized and beautiful place, like a well-run realm or palace.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that this larger topic is explained elsewhere?
questions.answer: To show that this section will focus only on one smaller example instead of the whole discussion.

questions.question: What season is used to display this truth on the earth?
questions.answer: Spring.

questions.question: In the imagined army, what makes the administration especially difficult?
questions.answer: There are four hundred thousand different groups, and each one needs separate care.

questions.question: Besides supplies, what else must the commander handle for every group?
questions.answer: He must also manage their instructions, release from service, and payments.

questions.question: What does the phrase about the “proper time” show?
questions.answer: It shows that the management is not only complete but also precisely timed.

questions.question: In the real example, who performs a similar work every spring?
questions.answer: An unseen hand performs it.

questions.question: What happens to around three hundred thousand species in autumn?
questions.answer: They are released from service and die, as part of the cycle of life.

questions.question: What truth is being shown through the example of spring?
questions.answer: The truth that Allah directs and manages the world with order and balance.

questions.question: What words in the passage show that this rule is both strong and caring?
questions.answer: It describes the administration as powerful and also merciful.

questions.question: What large parts of creation are governed together in this passage?
questions.answer: The skies, the natural forces, and the living beings on earth are governed together.

questions.question: What is the benefit of saying they help one another?
questions.answer: It shows that creation works in harmony, not as disconnected pieces.

questions.question: The world is compared to three organized places. What are they?
questions.answer: A kingdom, a city, and a palace.

questions.question: What does the comparison with a conquering ruler help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps the reader imagine how hard it would be to manage many different groups perfectly.

questions.question: Why is the number four hundred thousand important in the example?
questions.answer: It shows the huge variety and size of the army being managed.

questions.question: What details show that the ruler’s work is careful and just?
questions.answer: Every group gets its own proper supplies and treatment without error, neglect, or delay.

questions.question: What would happen if something without full power tried to control this system?
questions.answer: It would ruin the balance and produce disorder.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do we actually see every spring?
questions.answer: We see a hidden power bringing into being and organizing countless species like a vast army.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the autumn dismissal in the example from nature?
questions.answer: It means many living species complete their time and leave through death.

questions.question: Which two qualities are strongly emphasized in that administration?
questions.answer: Order and balance.

questions.question: What categories of created things are named to show the wide reach of this administration?
questions.answer: Celestial bodies, natural elements, and the creatures of the earth.

questions.question: How are these different created things connected in the passage?
questions.answer: They are made to support one another and are directed together.

questions.question: Why does the passage move from the huge universe to spring on earth?
questions.answer: To show a clear, understandable example of the same truth on one visible page of creation.

questions.question: What picture is used to explain the difficulty of this work?
questions.answer: The picture of a ruler managing a giant army made of many different groups.

questions.question: What makes the army in the comparison hard to manage?
questions.answer: Each group is different and needs its own supplies, orders, and timing.

questions.question: What does the perfect success of that imagined ruler point to?
questions.answer: It points to extraordinary power and skill that others do not have.

questions.question: According to the passage, why can ordinary causes not do this work?
questions.answer: Because they would only disturb the order and destroy the balance.

questions.question: What does the unseen hand do each spring?
questions.answer: It creates and organizes a splendid living army of four hundred thousand species.

questions.question: How is death presented in autumn?
questions.answer: It is shown as a release from duty for many species.

questions.question: What truth does this passage ask the reader to notice in creation?
questions.answer: It asks the reader to notice Allah’s ordering and governing of all things.

questions.question: What shows that this rule is universal and not limited to one place?
questions.answer: It covers the heavens, the elements, and the inhabitants of the earth.

questions.question: Why is equilibrium important in this passage?
questions.answer: Because it shows that creation is kept in measured balance, not chaos.

questions.question: What does the phrase about taking all necessary measures teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that everything needed for the system is carefully arranged.

questions.question: What is the purpose of comparing the world to a kingdom, city, and palace?
questions.answer: It highlights beauty, organization, and careful management.

questions.question: In that army example, what kinds of needs must be met for every group?
questions.answer: Their gear, clothing, instructions, release, and payment must all be handled properly.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the timing of this work?
questions.answer: It is done exactly when needed, without lateness or mix-up.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn about any other force trying to join this work?
questions.answer: It could not truly manage it and would only bring confusion.

questions.question: What natural event is described as a real example of this administration?
questions.answer: The coming of spring with the return and organization of many living species.

questions.question: What happens to three hundred thousand species in autumn, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They are sent away from their duties through death.
